collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks two adults)

collection.description: A friend mends a villager's net without asking, in a different knot: say thank you, or ask them to ask first.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) left (subject.his/her) fishing net drying on the rack with a big tear in it, meaning to fix it later. When (subject.he/she) comes back, (friend) has already mended it, without asking, and in a completely different style of knot from the one (subject) uses.

choices.label: Ask (friend) to Ask First Next Time

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "That's kind of you," says (subject). "But next time, could you ask first? I like doing my own mending." (friend)'s face falls a bit. "Oh. I just thought you'd be pleased." "I am, a bit," says (subject). "And I'd still like you to ask." (friend) nods slowly. Next time, (friend.he/she) asks. (subject) says yes about half the time.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: "Thank you," says (subject), looking at the strange knots. "I wasn't expecting that." (friend) beams. The net works fine. Better than fine, actually. (subject) studies the new knots and, a few weeks later, starts using them (subject.him/her)self. (subject.He/she) never tells (friend) that, mostly because (friend.he/she) would never hear the end of it.
